Dear Ms Ní Fhaoláin,

I assessed Ms Ó Súilleabháin today with her written consent; she has had sight of this report before release.

Background
Ms Ó Súilleabháin is a 55-year-old laboratory technician who has been with the company since 2009. She has been absent since 18-Aug-2026 following an admission to University Hospital Galway with a flare of Crohn's disease of the terminal ileum; her CRP rose to 48 mg/L at the time. She is now under Prof. Lucía Fernández-Hart (gastroenterology) and has started infliximab 5 mg/kg every 8 weeks. Her other history is Graves' disease, treated with radioactive iodine in 2015, and she takes levothyroxine 100 mcg for post-ablative hypothyroidism. Her GP, Dr Hope Achterberg (Claregalway Medical Centre), confirms her TSH is in range.

Current position
She reports 2-3 soft bowel motions a day, no frank rectal bleeding and fatigue of 5/10 by the end of a working day. Harvey-Bradshaw Index today is 3, consistent with remission. BP 128/76, weight stable. She is the main carer for her widowed father, Frank, who is 93 years old, and Rosie describes the night rota as the hardest part of her job at present.

Opinion and recommendations
She is fit to return to work from w/c 26/10/26 with the following temporary adjustments:
1. Phased return over 4 weeks, starting with 3 x 8-hour day shifts per week.
2. Exemption from night shifts for 3 months, then review; fatigue and infusion timing are the main issues.
3. Ready access to toilet facilities near the QC laboratory; no lone working at the remote silo sampling point.
4. Time off for infusions at the day ward to be treated as medical appointments.

I would hope that she can resume her full rota once her condition has been stable for 6 months. The Employment Equality Acts are likely to apply. I have not disclosed clinical detail beyond what is needed for these decisions.

Review: OH telephone review in 6 weeks (provisionally 4 Dec 2026).

Yours sincerely,

Dr Ciarán Graves MB MICGP LFOM
